originalTitle: Ethiopia's army says it has repelled attacks in first comment on fresh fighting
title: Keeping Everyone Safe in Beautiful Ethiopia!
content:
Hello from Africa!

Hi everyone! I'm your friendly news reporter for Africa, and I'm so excited to tell you about something happening in a very special country called Ethiopia. Ethiopia is a big, beautiful land in our amazing continent of Africa. It’s full of friendly people, wonderful animals, and fascinating stories. Today, we're going to talk about how grown-ups are working hard to keep everyone safe and happy there.

Where is Ethiopia?

Imagine a big map of Africa. Can you see the big horn shape on the eastern side? That's where Ethiopia is! It's a landlocked country, which means it doesn't have an ocean next to it, but it has lots of amazing mountains, green valleys, and even ancient lakes. It's a very old country, with a history that goes back thousands of years, like your great-great-grandparents' time and even before!

Did you know? Ethiopia is one of the oldest countries in the world! People have lived there for a very, very long time, building amazing things and telling wonderful stories.

What's Happening with the Grown-ups?

Sometimes, in any country, grown-ups have big disagreements. It's a bit like when you and your friend might argue over which game to play, but much, much bigger. In Ethiopia, there have been some big arguments between different groups of grown-ups. These arguments can sometimes get a little loud and messy, and that's not fun for anyone, especially for children.

Recently, these big arguments started up again. It means that some grown-ups were not agreeing on how to run things in their part of the country. When big disagreements happen, people can get worried. Everyone wants to live in a peaceful place where they feel safe. So, it’s important for someone to step in and help make things calm again.

The good news is that people are working to make sure everyone stays safe. It's like when a teacher helps friends sort out an argument in the playground – they want everyone to be happy and play nicely together. That’s what grown-ups in Ethiopia are trying to do for the whole country.

Who Helps Keep Everyone Safe?

Every country has special helpers called an "army" or "soldiers." These soldiers are like very big, very strong helpers whose job is to protect everyone in the country. They train very hard to keep people safe and make sure the country is stable. Their main goal is to keep peace and order, so that kids can go to school, families can grow food, and everyone can live without fear.

In Ethiopia, the army recently said that they stepped in when the big arguments started getting too much. They worked very hard to calm things down. Think of them as giant protectors. When things got a bit tricky and some grown-ups were causing trouble, the army was there to help make sure things didn't get out of control. They are trying to make sure that the disagreements don't hurt ordinary people and especially don't scare children.

They said they "repelled attacks," which means they pushed back the people who were causing problems and stopped them from hurting others. This is a very important job! It means they are helping to protect homes, schools, and hospitals, and most importantly, the people who live there. It's all about making sure that everyone can be safe and sound in their own communities.

Did you know? An army's job is not just to be strong, but also to help people when there are big problems, like keeping roads safe or even helping after a big storm!

Why is Peace Important?

Peace is like a warm, sunny day where everyone can play outside without any worries. When there is peace, kids can go to school every day and learn new things. Families can work together and share happy times. Businesses can grow, and people can build new houses and roads.

When there are big arguments, it can make it hard for everyone to do these important things. That's why grown-ups, both inside Ethiopia and from other countries, are all hoping for lasting peace. They want to see the arguments stop completely so that everyone can focus on making Ethiopia an even better place.

Imagine a playground where everyone is always kind and sharing – that's what peace feels like for a whole country! Everyone wants the people of Ethiopia to have that kind of peace, where they can laugh, learn, and grow without any big worries. It means people can be happy and safe in their homes and communities.

Did You Know? Fun Facts About Ethiopia!

Ethiopia is a truly amazing place! Let's learn some fun facts:

  • Coffee's Home: Do your parents drink coffee? Well, Ethiopia is where coffee was first discovered! It's like the birthplace of your morning brew!
  • Cool Animals: Ethiopia has some very special animals you won't find anywhere else! There are the Gelada baboons with their funny red chests, and the super rare Ethiopian wolves, who are beautiful and shy.
  • Unique Calendar: Ethiopia has its own calendar! It's a few years behind the one most of the world uses, and it has 13 months! Imagine having an extra month of holidays!
  • Ancient Churches: In some parts of Ethiopia, there are churches carved right out of giant rocks, underground! They are thousands of years old and look like something out of a fairy tale.
  • Beautiful Music: Ethiopian music is very special and has its own unique sound. It’s full of traditional instruments and lively rhythms that make you want to dance!

What We Hope For!

So, what does all this mean? It means that in beautiful Ethiopia, people are working hard to make sure everyone stays safe and happy. The army is playing its part in keeping things calm when big arguments happen. And everyone, everywhere, hopes that the grown-ups can talk things out and find peaceful ways to agree.

We wish for all the children in Ethiopia to wake up every day feeling safe, to go to school and learn, and to play with their friends. We hope that the arguments will stop for good, and that peace will shine brightly over all of Ethiopia. It's a land of wonder, and it deserves to be a land of peace and happiness for all its people!
summary: In Ethiopia, grown-up helpers called the army stepped in to keep everyone safe when big arguments happened, and everyone hopes for peace and happiness.
whyMatters: It's important because when everyone is safe and happy, kids can play and learn, and countries can grow strong together.

originalTitle: Tigray capital 'out of cash' as fighting escalates, resident tells BBC
title: Kind News for Mekelle: Our Friends Need Peace!
content:
Hello, Friends from Africa!

Hi everyone! It's your friendly African news reporter here. Today, we want to talk about a special place called Mekelle. It's a big city in a country called Ethiopia, right here on our amazing continent of Africa. Mekelle is a home to many children just like you. They love to play, go to school, and spend time with their families. But right now, things are a little bit tricky there. We heard some news from a grown-up who lives in Mekelle. They told us that even though the city feels calm right now, many people are feeling worried inside.

Meet Mekelle, a Beautiful City

Mekelle is a very important city in Ethiopia. It is the capital of a region called Tigray. A capital city is like the main hub, where many important offices and buildings are. Imagine your town or city. Mekelle is just like that, but maybe bigger! It has streets, markets, homes, and schools. Children there wake up, eat breakfast, and go about their day, just like you. Did you know? Ethiopia is one of the oldest countries in the world! It has a very long history and many amazing stories. It's also famous for its delicious coffee!

What is 'Fighting'?

Sometimes, grown-ups have very big disagreements. It's not like when you argue with your brother or sister over a toy. These are very serious disagreements between different groups of people. When these disagreements get too big, sometimes people start 'fighting.' This means there is trouble and sometimes things get very noisy and scary. It's a sad thing when people fight. This 'fighting' has been happening in the area around Mekelle. It makes people feel unsafe, even if the actual fighting is not right in their street. It makes everyone feel uneasy.

Money Trouble in the City

Our friend in Mekelle also told us something very important. They said that the city is 'out of cash.' What does that mean? Cash is money! It's the coins and notes that grown-ups use to buy things. We use money to buy yummy food, new clothes, toys, and even pay for school or doctors. Imagine if your parents couldn't get any money. It would be very hard to buy milk, bread, or fruits. It would be hard to buy new shoes for school. When a city is 'out of cash,' it means that banks might not have enough money. Or, it's hard for people to get their own money out of the bank. This makes it really hard for everyone to buy the things they need every single day. Did you know? Money helps us trade things easily! Before money, people used to trade things directly, like swapping a chicken for some maize!

Why Are People Stressed?

The grown-up in Mekelle said people are 'stressed.' What is 'stressed'? Feeling stressed is when you feel very worried or anxious about something. Maybe you feel stressed before a big test at school, or if you lose your favourite toy. Your stomach might feel funny, or you might find it hard to sleep. The people in Mekelle are stressed because of the fighting. They worry about their safety, about getting enough food, and about their families. They worry about when things will go back to normal. It’s a very natural feeling to be stressed when big, scary things are happening around you. Children there might feel stressed too, even if they don't know exactly why. It's a tough feeling.

How Does This Affect Children?

When there is fighting and no money, children are often affected the most. Schools might close down, which means children cannot learn and play with their friends. Sometimes, shops might not have enough food because people can't buy it, or it's hard for new food to come into the city. This means children might not get all the yummy, healthy food they need to grow strong. Playing outside might become scary, and parents might keep children indoors more often to keep them safe. This is very hard for little ones who love to run and explore and play games outside. Did you know? Playing and learning are super important for children to grow up happy and healthy! Every child deserves a chance to play and learn.

Working Towards Peace

The good news is that many people, big grown-ups from different countries and organisations, are working very hard to help. They want the fighting to stop. They are talking to each other to find a way for everyone to agree. They want peace to come back to Mekelle and the whole region of Tigray. Peace means everyone is safe, happy, and can go back to their normal lives. Did you know? The colour white often symbolises peace. We hope for a lot of peace in the world! Sometimes, people wear white to show they want peace.

My Wish for Mekelle

We hope that very soon, the people in Mekelle will feel safe again. We hope that banks will have plenty of cash, so everyone can buy what they need. We hope children can go back to school, play outside, and laugh loudly. It is important to remember that even in tough times, people are strong. The people of Mekelle are strong and kind. They are waiting for peace, just like we are. Let's send our kind thoughts and wishes to all the children and families in Mekelle. We hope that bright, sunny days are just around the corner for them, filled with peace and happiness. We want everyone in Mekelle to know that people care about them. We hope the fighting stops soon, and everyone can live without stress again, with smiles on their faces. Did you know? Africa is a continent with 54 amazing countries! Each one has its own special culture and beautiful people. Ethiopia is just one of these wonderful places. We are all one big family! We believe that with kindness and talking, grown-ups can solve their problems. Let's all wish for peace and happiness for our friends in Mekelle, Ethiopia. Thank you for listening!
summary: People in the city of Mekelle in Ethiopia are feeling worried and having trouble getting money because of some grown-up fighting, and everyone hopes for peace to come back soon.
whyMatters: It matters because when there is fighting and no money, children and families cannot live safely or buy what they need, and everyone deserves to live in peace.
